images.title: Pueblo Bonito seen from the east
images.creator: Joekoz451
images.licenseEvidence: The file page records a worldwide public-domain release by the photographer Joekoz451, with an unrestricted-use fallback.
images.alt: Standing masonry walls of Pueblo Bonito seen across desert scrub from the east.
images.caption: Pueblo Bonito seen from the east. Standing masonry preserves part of a great house built and altered through successive projects; the present remains cannot show every room as it existed in one year.
images.changes: None; original JPEG copied without cropping, retouching or recompression.

images.title: Nan Madol ruins in Pohnpei
images.creator: CT Snow
images.licenseEvidence: Commons identifies CT Snow as author and CC BY 2.0 as the license; its Flickr license review was recorded on 6 April 2008.
images.alt: Layered basalt masonry among vegetation at Nan Madol on Pohnpei.
images.caption: Basalt masonry at Nan Madol brings the labor of building into view. The wider settlement included artificial islets, waterways, residences and ceremonial places; this detail represents only part of that landscape.
images.changes: Wikimedia-generated 960-pixel preview; no local cropping or retouching.

images.title: Machu Picchu, Peru
images.creator: Sasha India
images.licenseEvidence: Commons identifies Sasha India as author and CC BY 2.0 as the license; its Flickr license review was recorded on 8 May 2021.
images.alt: Stone buildings and terraces of Machu Picchu on a steep green mountain ridge.
images.caption: Machu Picchu’s buildings and terraces occupy a steep ridge. Water collection, fountains and drainage made this built landscape possible alongside the better-known stone architecture.

images.title: “fei” = Yap Stone Money (2008)
images.creator: David Weekly
images.licenseEvidence: Commons identifies David Weekly as author; CC BY 2.0 was confirmed by its Flickr review on 4 September 2018.
images.alt: A large circular stone with a central opening standing among vegetation on Yap.
images.caption: A modern view of rai on Yap, photographed in 2008. The image records the object in a later setting; it does not depict the original quarrying, an ocean voyage or a nineteenth-century exchange.
images.changes: Wikimedia-generated 960-pixel JPEG preview; no local cropping or retouching.

images.title: Scaffolding for cutting stone money in Palau, 1910
images.creator: Elisabeth Krämer-Bannow
images.licenseEvidence: Commons identifies the photograph as public domain under life-plus-70 terms and as a work published before 1931 in the United States. Published in Wilhelm Müller, Yap, in Ergebnisse der Südsee-Expedition 1908–1910, Hamburg, 1914; page 234 digitized by Hamburg State and University Library.
images.alt: Historical black-and-white photograph of timber scaffolding against a rock face used to cut stone money in Palau.
images.caption: Timber scaffolding at a Palauan stone-money quarry, photographed during the 1908–1910 Hamburg expedition and published in 1914. This historical view shows a working arrangement at one place and time; it should not stand for every quarry or every period of rai production.
images.changes: Wikimedia-generated 960-pixel JPEG preview; no local cropping or retouching.

images.title: Mesa Verde: Cliff Palace detail
images.creator: Lisa Redfern / Lisafern
images.licenseEvidence: The photographer Lisafern explicitly dedicated this own-work image to the public domain under CC0 1.0 on its Commons file page.
images.alt: Masonry rooms and towers fitted beneath the sandstone alcove at Cliff Palace, Mesa Verde.
images.caption: Cliff Palace’s masonry fits the shelter and uneven ground of a rock alcove. Rooms and shared spaces formed a village within a wider landscape of mesa-top homes, fields and water sources.
images.changes: Wikimedia-generated 960-pixel JPEG preview; no local cropping or retouching.
